source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And they drew near{H7126} to Yerushalayim{H3389} and came{H935} to Beit{H1004} Pagei, to the Mount{H2022} of the Olives{H2132}, and Yeshua{H3442} sent{H7971} two{H8147} of his disciples{H8527}.

one_way_hebrew: בית פאגי — 'house of unripe figs' (Aramaic paggê; the Hebrew פַּג, H6291, is Song 2:13's word for the fig's green fruit). The Hebrew reader hears the place-name; the barren fig tree of vv. 18-19 is cursed on the road out of the House of Unripe Figs. In Greek Βηθφαγή is an opaque syllable-string.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק פ״ז (Perek 87) begins here.
The circulating transcription reads על ירושלם; Howard's text reads אל ירושלם, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:1): להר] בהר AH; ישו] omit H.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Go{H1980} to the fortress{H4013} which is opposite{H5227} you, and immediately you will find{H4672} one{H259} she-ass{H860} and one colt{H5895}; loose{H5425} them and bring{H935} them to me.

one_way_hebrew: והתירו — 'loose them': the verb of Ps 146:7, 'YHWH looses the bound' (מתיר אסורים); ms A even reads אתון אסורה, 'a she-ass BOUND.' A bound colt loosed for the king is Gen 49:11 enacted — Judah's ruler 'binding his colt (עירה) unto the vine' — and the ms writes עירה with the very consonants of Gen 49:11.
אתון (H860) and עיר (H5895) — Zech 9:9's own animal words (see v. 5).
greek_deviations: המבצר — 'the FORTRESS' (H4013, mibtsar), where Greek has κώμην ('village'). The Hebrew pictures a walled stronghold facing them.
translation_notes: מיד ('immediately') — the rabbinic-Hebrew adverb, used throughout this text where Greek has εὐθύς/εὐθέως.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads על המבצר and אתין; Howard's text reads אל המבצר and אתון, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:2): אליהם] להם G, omit H; נכחכם] נכחם H; אחת¹] + אסורה A ('bound'); אחת²] עמה A, + עמה BEFG ('with her'); אותם] אותה A ('her'); והביאום] והביאו אותם EF.

verses.translation: And if a man{H376} says{H559} any thing{H1697} to you, say{H559} to him that the master{H113} has need of them, and immediately he will let them go{H5800}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:3): יאמר] אמר A; לכם] אליכם ABDG, omit EF; אתהם] אתכם ABDEFG.

verses.translation: All{H3605} this{H2088} was to confirm{H6965} the word{H1697} of the prophet{H5030}, saying{H559}:

one_way_hebrew: לקיים (qiyyem, H6965) — the late-biblical Hebrew verb for confirming and establishing a word (Esth 9:21,27,31-32; Ezek 13:6; Ps 119:28,106). The 'fulfillment formula' of this gospel is native Jewish legal Hebrew — a word is 'made to stand' — not a rendering of Greek πληρόω ('fill').

verses.translation: Say{H559} to the daughter{H1323} of Zion{H6726}: Behold{H2009}, your king{H4428} comes{H935} to you, righteous{H6662} and saved{H3467} is he, lowly{H6041}, and riding{H7392} upon a she-ass{H860} and upon a colt{H5895}, the foal{H1121} of a she-ass{H860}.

one_way_hebrew: צדיק ונושע הוא — 'righteous and SAVED is he': Zech 9:9's central clause, which GREEK MATTHEW OMITS entirely (it jumps from 'thy King cometh unto thee' to 'meek'). The Hebrew Matthew carries Zechariah's full line; a translator working from the Greek could not have restored what his source never contained.
The opening אמרו לבת ציון is Isa 62:11 verbatim (אמרו לבת ציון הנה ישעך בא) — the same Isaiah-Zechariah weave as Greek Matthew, but in the prophets' own consonants.
ונושע is the nifal of ישע — the root of the rider's own name (ישו״ע): the king who comes 'saved' carries salvation in his name.
greek_deviations: The animals: MT Zech 9:9 has חמור ('ass')... עיר בן אתנות ('colt, foal of she-asses'); this text reads אתון both times — 'upon a SHE-ASS and upon a colt, the foal of a she-ass' — the mother and her foal of v. 2, named consistently. Howard's own introduction singles out Shem Tov's handling of the ass and colt: the Hebrew text and its narrative (v. 7, 'he rode upon HER') hold together where Greek Matthew's two-animal quotation famously strains (see v. 7). Mss AEFG assimilate the first אתון back to MT's חמור, and BEF the second to אתנות — later copyists correcting toward the Masoretic wording, the base text standing independent.
translation_notes: ורוסב — a scribal metathesis for ורוכב ('and riding'), as mss ABCDEFG read; the translation follows the sense.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:5): יבא] בא EF; ונושע הוא] omit G; ורוסב] ורוכב ABCDEFG; אתון¹] חמור AEFG; אתון²] אתונות BEF.

The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'Say to the descendants of Yisrael... humble: sitting upon the female donkey, even a young ass — her foal,' likewise without Greek Matthew's omission of 'righteous and saved,' but with its own recasting of the address.

verses.translation: And they went{H1980} and did{H6213} as Yeshua{H3442} commanded{H6680} them.

one_way_hebrew: ויעשו כאשר ציום — the Torah's obedience formula (Exod 7:6, ויעש... כאשר צוה יהוה אתם; Exod 39-40 passim). The disciples obey in the Pentateuch's own cadence.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:6): ישו] omit G.

verses.translation: And they brought{H935} the she-ass{H860} and the colt{H5895}, and Yeshua{H3442} rode{H7392} upon her{H5921}; and the others{H312} placed{H7760} their vessels{H3627} and their garments{H4403} on them, and went up{H5927} above{H4605}.

greek_deviations: וירכב עליה — 'he rode upon HER,' singular and feminine: the she-ass, her foal alongside. Greek Matthew reads ἐπεκάθισεν ἐπάνω αὐτῶν, 'he sat upon THEM' — the reading that has drawn centuries of mockery about riding two animals at once. The Hebrew text never had the problem: the plural עליהם in this verse belongs to the garments laid on the two animals, and the rider sits on one. The Greek's αὐτῶν reads like a translator's blur of exactly this Hebrew distinction.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:7): no doctrinally significant variants recorded.

verses.translation: And many{H7227} of the company{H2267} were spreading{H6566} their garments{H4403} in the road{H1870}, and others{H312} cut branches{H6057} of the trees{H6086} and cast{H7993} them before{H6440} him and behind{H310} him.

translation_notes: הסודרנא — an unexplained form in the base ms (perhaps built on סודר, the rabbinic word for a cloth); mss ABDEFG read כורתים ('cutting'), which Howard's English follows and the translation adopts.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:8): הסודרנא] כורתים ABDEFG; ואחרים] ורבים G.

verses.translation: crying out{H7121}, saying{H559}: Hoshana{H3467}, Savior{H3467} of the world{H5769}! Blessed{H1288} is he who comes{H935} in the name{H8034} of YHWH{H3068}! Hoshana{H3467}, our Savior{H3467} — be glorified{H6286} in the heavens{H8064} and in the earth{H776}!

one_way_hebrew: הושענא — the crowd's cry is Ps 118:25-26 alive in its own tongue: הושיעה נא ('save now!')... ברוך הבא בשם יהוה. In the Hebrew the cry, the psalm, and the Name cohere; Greek ὡσαννά is a transliterated fossil that Greek readers could no longer parse.
תתפאר (H6286) — 'be glorified': Isaiah's verb for God glorifying himself in Israel (Isa 44:23; 49:3; 60:21; 61:3).
greek_deviations: The Hebrew crowd hails מושיע העולם — 'the Savior of the WORLD' — where Greek Matthew has 'Hosanna to the Son of David.' 'Savior of the world' is elsewhere a Johannine title (John 4:42; 1 John 4:14); here it stands in Hebrew Matthew's triumphal entry. And for Greek's 'Hosanna in the highest' the Hebrew reads 'be glorified in the heavens and in the earth.'
textual_notes: First occurrence in this chapter of ה״ — the ms writes ה״ ('The Name') for the Tetragrammaton, here inside the Ps 118:26 quotation.
Howard's apparatus (21:9): הושענא] הושענה A; מושיע העולם] מושיענו עולם EF, מושיע המלך העולם B.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} after{H310} this, when Yeshua{H3442} entered{H935} Yerushalayim{H3389}, all{H3605} the city{H5892} trembled{H2729}, saying{H559}: Who{H4310} is this{H2088}?

one_way_hebrew: חרדה (H2729) — 'trembled': Isaac's trembling (ויחרד... חרדה גדלה, Gen 27:33), Sinai's (Exod 19:18), the city elders' before Samuel (1 Sam 16:4, ויחרדו... לקראתו, with the same anxious question). Greek ἐσείσθη ('was shaken') is seismic; the Hebrew is the fear-word of a city meeting something holy.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads מע הוא זה; Howard's text reads מי הוא זה, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:10): חרדה] + ירושלם ABEF.

verses.translation: And the people{H5971} said{H559} to one another{H2088}: This is Yeshua{H3442} the prophet{H5030} from Nazareth, which is in Galil{H1551}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:11): the mss spell the place-name variously — מנאזריאל A, מנזריאל B, מנזארת DEF, מנזריל G (base מנאזא״ריל); Howard's English renders 'from Nazareth.'

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} entered{H935} the house{H1004} of YHWH{H3068} and found{H4672} there{H8033} the buyers{H7069} and the sellers{H4376}, and he overturned{H2015} the tables{H3871} of the money-changers and the seats{H4186} of the sellers{H4376} of doves{H3123}.

one_way_hebrew: בית ה״ — 'the house of YHWH': the Tanakh's standing name for the Temple (1 Kgs 6:1; Ps 122:1,9), written with the reverent ה״ for the Name. Greek has ἱερὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ('temple of God'); only the Hebrew calls it by its scriptural name.
ויהפוך (H2015) — the overthrow verb of Sodom (Gen 19:25) and Jonah's Nineveh (Jonah 3:4): the tables are not just tipped, they are 'overturned' with judgment's own word.

השולחנים — shulchani, the Mishnah's word for a money-changer (m.Sheqalim 1:3, the shulchanim who sat in the Sanctuary precincts from Adar 25!); Greek κολλυβιστής is itself a Semitic loanword (from qolbon). The Hebrew is at home; the Greek borrows.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:12): בית] בבית AEF; וימצא] ויוצא A; שם] משם A; והמושבות] ומושבותם A; היונים] omit A, יונים G.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: It is written: My house{H1004} shall be called{H7121} a house of prayer{H8605} for all{H3605} the peoples{H5971} — but you{H859} have made{H6213} it a cave{H4631} of violent men{H6530}.

one_way_hebrew: כי ביתי בית תפלה יקרא לכל העמים — Isa 56:7 letter-for-letter, INCLUDING 'for all the peoples' (לכל העמים), which Greek Matthew drops (only Mark 11:17 keeps πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν). The Hebrew Matthew carries the whole verse of Isaiah where Greek Matthew carries a torn-off half — and it agrees with Mark against Greek Matthew in doing so.
מערת פריצים — Jer 7:11 verbatim (המערת פרצים היה הבית הזה). Isaiah's clause and Jeremiah's answer each in their own consonants: quotation, not translation.
כתיב — the Aramaic-Hebrew citation formula of the study-house ('it is written'), the scribe's native way of introducing Scripture.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription doubles the object (אותם אותה); Howard's text reads עשיתם אותה alone, corrected here.

verses.translation: And the blind{H5787} and the lame{H6455} drew near{H7126} to him in the Sanctuary{H4720}, and he healed{H7495} them.

one_way_hebrew: עורים ופסחים — 'the blind and the lame': the pair of 2 Sam 5:8, where 'the blind and the lame' are barred from the house (בית). Here the Son of David heals exactly this pair inside the Sanctuary — the old exclusion reversed in its own two words. Greek τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοί translates the pair without the Davidic echo.

verses.translation: And the chiefs{H1419} of the sages{H2450} and the priests{H3548} came{H935} to see{H7200} the wonders{H6382} that he did{H6213}; and the boys{H5288} were crying out{H7121} in the Sanctuary{H4720} and saying{H559}: Praised{H7623} be the Son{H1121} of El{H410}! And the sages{H2450} mocked{H3932}.

one_way_hebrew: ילעגו (H3932) — 'they mocked': the passion-psalm's verb, 'all they that see me laugh me to scorn (ילעגו לי)' (Ps 22:8). The chapter that begins with Ps 118's blessing already sounds Ps 22's scorn.
ישתבח (H7623) — the hitpael 'be praised', the very form that opens the synagogue doxology (ישתבח שמך); Ps 106:47, להשתבח בתהלתך.
greek_deviations: The boys cry 'Praised be the SON OF EL' (ישתבח בן האל) — where Greek Matthew has 'Hosanna to the Son of David.' No Shem Tov ms assimilates it: the children's cry in the Hebrew text confesses divine sonship in the Sanctuary itself, and it is this that the sages mock.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:15): ויבואו] ויצאו EF; החכמים והכהנים] transposed ABDEF; לראות] omit A.

verses.translation: And they said{H559} to him: Do you not hear{H8085} what{H4100} these{H428} are saying{H559}? And he answered{H6030} them and said{H559}: I hear{H8085} them. Have you not read{H7121}: From the mouth{H6310} of babes{H5768} and sucklings{H3243} you founded{H3245} strength{H5797}?

one_way_hebrew: מפי עוללים ויונקים יסדת עוז — Ps 8:3 in the Masoretic text's own words: 'thou hast founded STRENGTH (עז).' Greek Matthew quotes the Septuagint instead — κατηρτίσω αἶνον, 'thou hast perfected PRAISE.' Here the two textual streams part cleanly: the Greek gospel stands on the Greek psalter, the Hebrew gospel on the Hebrew psalm. A back-translator from Greek would have written שבח or תהלה ('praise'); this text has עוז because its psalm is the MT.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads ואמרו; Howard's text reads ויאמרו, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:16): לו] omit A; אומרים] יאמרו A; אלו¹] אליו A; להם] אליהם G; ויאמר] omit A; אלו²] omit A.

verses.translation: And he left{H5800} and went{H1980} outside{H2351} to Beit Chananyah, and went there{H8033}; and there he was expounding{H1875} to them concerning the kingdom{H4438} of El{H410}.

one_way_hebrew: בית חנניא — Bethany as a Hebrew name, 'the house of Chananyah' ('YH has been gracious'); Greek Βηθανία transliterates syllables the Hebrew still reads.
דורש (H1875) — 'expounding': the darash of the study-house (whence midrash), Ezra's verb (Ezra 7:10, לדרש את תורת יהוה).
greek_deviations: 'And there he was expounding to them concerning the kingdom of El' — absent from Greek Matthew, which says only that he lodged there. The Hebrew adds a teaching notice in rabbinic idiom (cf. Luke 21:37's nightly teaching).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:17): ויעזוב] + אותם ABDEFG ('he left THEM'); חנניא] חנניה BCDEFG; וילך²] וילן ABDEFG ('and he LODGED there' — matching Greek ηὐλίσθη; the base text repeats וילך).

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} in the morning{H1242}, he returned{H7725} to the city{H5892} hungry{H7457}.

And he saw{H7200} one{H259} fig tree{H8384} beside{H681} the road{H1870} and approached{H5066} it, and found{H4672} nothing on it except{H7535} the leaves{H5929} alone{H905}. And he said{H559} to it: Let no fruit{H6529} come forth{H3318} from you forever{H5769}. And the fig tree{H8384} dried up{H3001} immediately.

one_way_hebrew: The scene is Jer 8:13 enacted: 'there shall be no figs on the fig tree (אין תאנים בתאנה), and the leaf shall fade.' Leaves without figs is Jeremiah's picture of a nation ripe for judgment; the curse ותיבש speaks Jeremiah's sentence over it. The road runs from בית פאגי, the 'house of unripe figs' (v. 1).
עלים לבד — 'leaves only': the first fig leaves in Scripture covered fruitlessness too (Gen 3:7).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:19): וירא] ויאר G; אחת] omit G; בה] + תאנים EF; לבד] בלבד B; התאנה מיד] omit G.

verses.translation: And the disciples{H8527} saw{H7200} it and marveled{H8539}, and said{H559}: How{H349} did the fig tree{H8384} dry up{H3001} immediately?

one_way_hebrew: ויתמהו (H8539) — 'they marveled': Hab 1:5's imperative (התמהו תמהו) and Gen 43:33; the astonishment-verb of Scripture.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:20): מיד] omit G; ויאמרו] לאמר G; ויתמהו] + מאד G.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} and said{H559} to them: If there is in you faith{H530} without{H1097} doubt, you will do{H6213} not only{H905} to the fig tree{H8384}; but if you say{H559} to this{H2088} mountain{H2022}: Depart{H4185}, and go{H935} into the sea — it will be done{H6213}.

one_way_hebrew: שימוש — 'that it DEPART' (מוש, H4185): Isaiah's mountain-verb, 'for the mountains shall depart (ימושו) and the hills be removed, but my kindness shall not depart (ימוש) from thee' (Isa 54:10). The mountain-moving word of faith is spoken in the very verb Scripture reserves for mountains departing; Greek ἄρθητι ('be lifted') loses the allusion.
ספק ('doubt') — rabbinic Hebrew's own category (safeq); biblical Hebrew has no noun for doubt, and this text reaches for the living word.
translation_notes: בם — the base ms reads בם ('into them'); mss AEF read בים ('into the sea'), DG כן ('so'). The sense requires בים, which the translation follows (Greek: 'be thou cast into the sea').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:21): בם] בים AEF, כן DG; ויען...להם] ויאמר להם ישו G.

verses.translation: And all{H3605} that you ask{H7592} in prayer{H8605}, being believers{H539}, you will receive{H6901}.

one_way_hebrew: תקבלון (H6901, qabal) — again the late-Hebrew receiving verb (Esth 4:4; 9:23), the natural register of a Second-Temple Hebrew author.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:22): וכל] ובכל BEFG.

verses.translation: And he came{H935} to the Sanctuary{H4720} to teach{H3925}, and the sages{H2450} and the priests{H3548} and the officers{H7101} of the people{H5971} drew near{H7126} to him, saying{H559}: By what{H335} power{H3581} do you do{H6213} this{H2088} might{H2428}?

one_way_hebrew: קציני העם — 'officers of the people': Isaiah's word for Jerusalem's rulers (קציני סדם, Isa 1:10; Isa 3:6-7; Judg 11:6). Greek πρεσβύτεροι ('elders') is administrative; קצין carries Isaiah's edge.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק פ״ט (Perek 89) begins here.
The circulating transcription reads העמ; Howard's text reads העם, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:23): תעשה] + ומי נתן לך ABDEFGH ('and who gave [it] to you' — BEF without לך): all other mss carry the question's second half, matching the Greek; the base ms alone runs short.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them and said{H559} to them: I also{H1571} will ask{H7592} of you one{H259} question{H7596}, and if you tell{H559} me it, I also will tell you by what{H335} power{H3581} I do{H6213} this.

one_way_hebrew: שאלה (H7596) — Hannah's and Esther's word for the one petition (1 Sam 1:17; Esth 5:6-7), cognate to the verb אשאל beside it — native Hebrew figura etymologica.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads אנט three times; Howard's text reads אני, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:24): שאלה אחת] דבר אחד ABDEFGH; לי אותה] אותה לי BDG, אותו לי CEF.

verses.translation: The immersion{H2881} of Yochanan{H3110} — from where{H370} was it, from the heavens{H8064} or from men{H376}? And they were vexed{H6087} among{H996} themselves, saying{H559}: What{H4100} shall we say{H559}? If we say: From the heavens — he will say to us: Why{H4100} did you not believe{H539} in him?

one_way_hebrew: טבילה — the immersion, from טבל (H2881), Naaman's sevenfold dipping (2 Kgs 5:14) and the rabbinic tevilah; Greek βάπτισμα is the loan-translation of this Hebrew institution.
ויתעצבו (H6087) — 'they were grieved/vexed': Gen 6:6's and Gen 45:5's inward pain-verb; Greek διελογίζοντο ('they reasoned') is bloodless beside it.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:25): מה נאמר] omit ADEFGH — the base text's extra 'What shall we say?' drops out of most mss toward the Greek.

verses.translation: And if we say: From men{H376} — we fear{H3372} the company{H2267}, for all{H3605} of them believe{H539} that Yochanan{H3110} was a prophet{H5030}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:26): החבורה] החבורות AH; מן החבורה] מהחבורה A; מן האנשים] מהאנשים EF.

textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads אנט; Howard's text reads אני, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:27): ויאמרו] + לו H; לא¹] איני A; ויאמר] + להם H.

verses.translation: In that{H1931} evening{H6153} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: What{H4100} does it seem{H7200} to you? A certain{H259} man{H376} had two{H8147} sons{H1121}; and he approached{H5066} the one{H259} and said{H559} to him: Go{H1980}, my son{H1121}, today{H3117} to work{H5647} my vineyard{H3754}.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew sets the scene — 'in that evening Yeshua said to his disciples' — a narrative frame Greek Matthew lacks; the parable is told in the evening after the Sanctuary confrontation.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ׳ (Perek 90) begins here.
The circulating transcription reads בנט; Howard's text reads בני, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:28): בערב] בעת A; מה נראה] הנראה DG; האחד] לאחד D; היום לעבוד] transposed A; לעבוד] עבוד G; כרמי] לכרמי A, בכרמי BDEFG.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to him: I do not want{H7521} to. But afterwards he repented{H5162} and went{H1980}.

one_way_hebrew: נחם (H5162) — the Tanakh's repenting verb (Exod 32:14; Joel 2:13; Jonah 3:9-10); the whole parable turns on it (vv. 29, 32). Greek μεταμεληθείς translates.
translation_notes: ואח״כ — the ms abbreviates ואחר כך ('and afterwards') with gershayim.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} likewise{H3644} to the other{H312}, and he answered{H6030} him: Here am I{H2009}, my lord{H113} — but he did not go{H1980}.

one_way_hebrew: הנני — 'Here am I': Abraham's answer (Gen 22:1), Samuel's (1 Sam 3:4), Isaiah's (Isa 6:8) — Scripture's word of instant readiness, put in the mouth of the son who never goes. The irony is Hebrew to the bone; Greek ἐγώ, κύριε keeps the scene but not the loaded word.
translation_notes: אדו׳ — the ms abbreviates אדוני ('my lord') with a geresh.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:30): הנני אדו׳] transposed A.

verses.translation: Who{H4310} of the two{H8147} did{H6213} the will{H7522} of the father{H1}? And they said{H559} to him: The first{H7223}. And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: Amen{H543}, I say to you that the violent{H6530} and the harlots{H6948} will precede{H6923} you into the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: פריצים (H6530) — the same word as v. 13's 'cave of פריצים' (Jer 7:11). The Hebrew chapter binds the Temple-cleansing and this saying with one word: the 'violent men' who profaned the house are nearer the kingdom than its keepers. Greek severs the thread (λῃσταί in v. 13, τελῶναι 'tax collectors' here).
קדשות (H6948) — the Torah's word for cult-harlots (Gen 38:21-22; Deut 23:18; Hos 4:14): not Greek πόρναι in Hebrew dress but the Tanakh's own charged term.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads במבלכות; Howard's text reads במלכות, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:31): ישו] omit EF.

verses.translation: For Yochanan{H3110} came{H935} to you in the way{H1870} of righteousness{H6666} and you did not believe{H539}; the violent{H6530} and the harlots{H6948} came and believed{H539} in him, but you saw{H7200} and did not return{H8666} in repentance; even afterwards{H310} you did not repent{H5162} to believe{H539} in him. Whoever has ears{H241} to hear{H8085}, let him hear{H8085} — in disgrace{H2781}.

one_way_hebrew: דרך צדקה — 'the way of righteousness': Prov 8:20 (בארח צדקה אהלך) and 12:28; a Proverbs phrase in a Proverbs mouth.

חזרתם בתשובה — 'return in repentance': the rabbinic idiom itself (חזר בתשובה), the living Hebrew term for repentance; Greek μετεμελήθητε renders one layer of it. Together with נחמתם (H5162) the verse stacks Hebrew's two repentance-verbs.
greek_deviations: The closing call — 'whoever has ears to hear, let him hear, in disgrace' — is absent from Greek Matthew 21:32. The ears-formula with the stinging tail בחרפה ('in disgrace', H2781) is unique to the Hebrew here (ms A softens to בחכמה, 'in wisdom').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:32): יוחנן] omit EF; המנתם] האמינתם A, האמנתם BDEFG; באו הפריצים] בו והפריצים ABDEFG ('you did not believe IN HIM; and the violent...'); והאמינו] האמינו ABDEG; נחמתם] חזרתם G; בחרפה] בחכמה A.
המנתם — a defective spelling of האמנתם ('you believed'), as the variants show.

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527} and to the company of the Jews{H3064}: Hear{H8085} now{H4994} the parable{H4912} of the sower{H2232}. A certain{H259} honored{H3513} man{H120} planted{H5193} a vineyard{H3754} and fenced{H1443} it round about{H5439}, and built{H1129} a tower{H4026} in its midst{H8432} and also hewed{H2672} a winepress{H3342} in it, and entrusted{H6485} it to workers{H5647} and went{H1980} on his way{H1870}.

one_way_hebrew: The verse quotes Isaiah's vineyard-song in Isaiah's own consonants: ויבן מגדל בתוכו וגם יקב חצב בו — Isa 5:2's וַיִּבֶן מִגְדָּל בְּתוֹכוֹ וְגַם־יֶקֶב חָצֵב בּוֹ, letter for letter. Greek Matthew translates the clause (ὤρυξεν ἐν αὐτῷ ληνόν); the Hebrew Matthew carries Isaiah's very words, so that no hearer could miss whose vineyard this is (Isa 5:7: 'the vineyard of YHWH of hosts is the house of Israel').
סיעה — 'the company (si'ah) of the Jews': a rabbinic-Hebrew collective noun no translator from Greek would coin.
translation_notes: משל הזורע — 'the parable of the sower/planter': the Hebrew heads the vineyard parable with the planter's title where Greek has only 'another parable.'
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק צ״א (Perek 91) begins here.

Howard's note (21:33-46): 'Omit Brit. Lib. ms and C. Our basic text for these vss is D' — the whole parable is supplied from ms D and printed by Howard in parentheses; the base London ms lost the passage.
The circulating transcription doubles אותו; Howard's text reads וגדר אותו מסביב, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:34 within the parable): אל¹] את EG, omit B.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} at the time{H6256} of gathering{H622} the produce{H8393}, he sent{H7971} his servants{H5650} to the workers{H5647} to receive{H6901} his produce{H8393}.

one_way_hebrew: תבואה (H8393) — the Torah's produce word (Lev 25:3,7); אסוף — the ingathering verb of Exod 23:16 (חג האסיף). The rent is described in the Torah's agricultural vocabulary.

verses.translation: And the workers{H5647} took{H3947} his servants{H5650}, and beat{H5221} the one{H259}, and killed{H2026} the second{H8145}, and the third{H7992} they stoned{H5619} with stones{H68}.

one_way_hebrew: סקלו באבנים (H5619) — stoning is Israel's own execution (Lev 24:16), and it is precisely how the prophet Zechariah died in the Temple court (2 Chr 24:21, וירגמהו אבן) — the murder this gospel names two chapters on (23:35). The Hebrew verb plants that seed here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:35): והשלישי סקלו באבנים] ויסקל את השלישי G.

verses.translation: And he sent{H7971} again{H5750} more{H7227} servants{H5650} than the first{H7223}, and they did{H6213} to them likewise{H3644}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:36): רבים] omit A; מהראשונים] omit EF.

verses.translation: At the end{H5490} of the matter{H1697} he sent{H7971} them his son{H1121}, saying{H559}: Perhaps{H194} they will stand in awe{H3372} of my son{H1121}.

one_way_hebrew: סוף דבר — 'the end of the matter': Ecclesiastes' closing formula verbatim (Eccl 12:13, סוף דבר הכל נשמע). The Hebrew narrator paces his story with Qohelet's own hinge-phrase; Greek ὕστερον ('afterward') is a bare adverb.

יראו (H3372) — 'fear/revere': the Torah's awe-verb (Lev 19:3, איש אמו ואביו תיראו — a son is what one fears). Greek ἐντραπήσονται ('respect') translates the idea, the Hebrew speaks the commandment's language.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads אולט; Howard's text reads אולי, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:37): דבר] הדבר ABEF; לאמר] ויאמר G.

verses.translation: And the workers{H5647} saw{H7200} his son{H1121} and said{H559} each man{H376} to his fellow{H7453}: This is{H2088} the heir{H3423}; come{H1980}, let us kill him{H2026} and inherit{H3423} his inheritance{H5159}.

one_way_hebrew: לכו ונהרגהו — Joseph's brothers' plot verbatim: 'Come now, and let us kill him' (ועתה לכו ונהרגהו, Gen 37:20). The sons of Israel speak against the beloved son in the very words their fathers used against Joseph; Greek δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν translates the sentence but cannot quote it.

איש אל רעהו — Gen 11:3's and Exod 25:20's mutual idiom; נחלה (H5159) — the covenant inheritance word (the vineyard as Israel's נחלה, cf. 1 Kgs 21:3, Naboth's vineyard: 'YHWH forbid... that I should give the inheritance of my fathers').

And now{H6258}, when the owner{H1167} of the vineyard{H3754} comes{H935}, what{H4100} will he do{H6213} to them?

verses.translation: And they answered{H6030} him, saying{H559}: The evil{H7451} ones — he will destroy{H6} them with evil{H7451}, and his vineyard{H3754} he will give{H5414} to other{H312} workers{H5647} who will give him the portion{H2506} of his produce{H8393} in its time.

one_way_hebrew: הרעים יאבדם ברעה — the Hebrew paronomasia (ra'im... ra'ah) that even Greek Matthew's κακοὺς κακῶς preserves as a fossil: the wordplay is native here and imitated there.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: Have you not read{H7121} the Scripture{H3789}: The stone{H68} the builders{H1129} rejected{H3988} has become{H1961} the head{H7218} of the corner{H6438}; from YHWH{H3068} this{H2063} came to be — it is marvelous{H6381} in our eyes{H5869}?

one_way_hebrew: Ps 118:22-23 verbatim, with מאת ה״ — the Name itself — where Greek has παρὰ κυρίου. The chapter is framed by Ps 118: the crowd sang its vv. 25-26 at the gates (v. 9), and the parable closes on its vv. 22-23 — the Hallel psalm of the festival pilgrims, quoted twice at its two hinges. Only in Hebrew is it visibly one psalm.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (21:42): נפלאת] נפלאות B; מאת...בעינינו] omit G.

verses.translation: Therefore{H2063} I say{H559} to you that the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} will be torn{H7167} from upon you and given{H5414} to a nation{H1471} producing{H6213} fruit{H6529}.

one_way_hebrew: שתתקרע... ותנתן — 'will be TORN from you and GIVEN to...': Samuel's oracle to Saul in its exact two-verb structure: 'YHWH has torn (קרע) the kingdom of Israel from you this day, and has given it (ונתנה) to a neighbour of thine' (1 Sam 15:28; cf. 1 Kgs 11:11). Greek ἀρθήσεται ('will be taken away') loses the tearing; the Hebrew reader hears Saul's sentence falling on the vineyard's keepers.
textual_notes: No Shem Tov ms softens שתתקרע; the reading is uniform.

verses.translation: And he who falls{H5307} upon this{H2063} stone{H68} will be cast down{H1760}, and he on whom it falls{H5307} will be split apart.

one_way_hebrew: ידחה... יפול — the pair of Ps 118:13 (דחה דחיתני לנפל, 'thou hast thrust sore at me that I might fall'): the stone-verse continues speaking in the vocabulary of the very psalm just quoted.
יסדק — rabbinic Hebrew's 'split, crack' (sadaq), a living-language verb with no biblical Strong's; Greek λικμήσει ('will grind to powder') renders it loosely.
greek_deviations: Greek Matt 21:44 is missing from important Greek witnesses (D, some Old Latin) and bracketed in critical editions as a possible import from Luke 20:18; the Shem Tov Hebrew carries the verse without any recorded variant — in this family it is native text, not an intruder.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads האבנ and ידתה; Howard's text reads האבן and ידחה, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (21:44): יסדק] יפסק A; ואשר יפול] והנופל EF; ידחה] יראה EF.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 21 in the Shem Tov Hebrew: (1) The Zech 9:9 quotation (v. 5) keeps Zechariah's central clause צדיק ונושע הוא ('righteous and SAVED is he'), which Greek Matthew omits — and reads 'upon a she-ass (אתון) and upon a colt, the foal of a she-ass,' so that v. 7 can say 'he rode upon HER' (עליה, singular): the Hebrew never has Greek Matthew's 'he sat upon THEM.' Howard's own introduction flags Shem Tov's handling of the ass and colt; mss AEFG/BEF assimilate the nouns back toward the Masoretic חמור/אתנות. (2) The Temple word (v. 13) quotes Isa 56:7 WITH 'for all the peoples' — agreeing with Mark 11:17 and Isaiah against Greek Matthew's shortened quote — and Jer 7:11's מערת פריצים; the same word פריצים then returns in v. 31 ('the violent and the harlots will precede you'), a one-word thread Greek breaks (λῃσταί/τελῶναι). (3) The children in the Sanctuary cry 'Praised be the SON OF EL' (v. 15) where Greek has 'Hosanna to the Son of David,' and the Ps 8:3 answer (v. 16) reads the MT's יסדת עוז ('founded STRENGTH') against Greek Matthew's Septuagintal 'perfected praise' — a clean split between the Hebrew and Greek Bibles. (4) The crowd's cry (v. 9) is Ps 118:25-26 in its own tongue with the Name (בשם ה״), hailing 'the Savior of the WORLD'; Ps 118 then returns at v. 42 (stone, מאת ה״) and echoes in v. 44 (דחה/נפל, Ps 118:13) — the Hallel frames the chapter. (5) The vineyard parable (v. 33) quotes Isa 5:2 letter-for-letter (ויבן מגדל בתוכו וגם יקב חצב בו); the tenants plot in Gen 37:20's exact words (לכו ונהרגהו, v. 38); and the sentence (v. 43) falls in Samuel's two verbs to Saul — torn (תתקרע) and given (ותנתן) to another (1 Sam 15:28). Verses 33-46 are lost from the base London ms and ms C; Howard prints them in parentheses from ms D. (6) The mountain-moving saying (v. 21) uses Isa 54:10's mountain-verb מוש ('depart'). (7) Perek marks: vv. 1 (87), 10 (88), 23 (89), 28 (90), 33 (91).
